reason: The verse longs to set the mind unmoving (பேராமலே இருத்தி) in the one awareness; mind-wandering and happiness is a shared topic, but the verse claims nothing about mood.
The verse calls pilgrimage and the family god (குலதெய்வம்) forms of desire; it says nothing about adaptation of happiness to gains and losses.

reason: A praise of Siva as supreme guru (சிவனே பரமகுரு); no claim about perception.
text_issue: Unit ends mid-word (நவநீத) running into the next unit.

reason: A snake moving from the banyan hole to the pipal hole (ஆலடிப் பொந்து, அரசடிப் பொந்து); any link to autonomic control rests wholly on a cipher the Tamil does not fix.

The verse vouches that an earlier book told the drugs and salts (சரக்கு) and melts truly, without a lie (பொய்யப்பா சொல்லவில்லை); it names no preparation or effect, so the heavy-metal poisoning finding shares only the topic of Siddha materia medica.
The verse mocks claimants of kaya-kalpa (காயகாயம்) as frauds sustained by ganja and opium; it makes no claim about Siddha decoctions against disease, so the trial finding is only topical.
The verse names arsenic and alchemical drugs (பாடாணம், செந்தூரம்) whose effect is burning; nothing concerns curcumin.
The verse rebukes those who call the breast maya and urges inner examination (உண்மையகத் தேர்வீர்); no claim about perception as prediction.

The verse gives a breathing practice with counts (ரேசி, வாங்கி, ஊதி; twelve and sixteen) whose result is that the subtle body subsides (புரியட்டம் அடங்கிற்று); HRV is not what it claims, and the numbers' referents rest on cipher glosses.
The verse says what is born is breath (பிராணன்), neither female nor male; it makes no claim that a stock of breaths sets lifespan, so only breath and death are shared.
The verse decodes the moon and sun channels and promises trance from kumbhaka (கும்பித்துச் சொக்குவீரே); sleep and brain-waste clearance are unrelated.
Inner anklet and conch sounds and the breath (வாசி); no claim of precognition or psychic power.
The verse reminds that Death (காலன்) can seize one mid-pleasure, leaving a corpse (செத்த சவம்); it is itself a death reminder but claims nothing about how such reminders shift attitudes.
The verse longs to throw off the rice-bag body (சோற்றுத் துருத்தி); nothing about mantra repetition.

The verse says silence-knowledge (மவுன ஞானம்) cannot be told by the mouth; a theory of meditation loosening predictive models shares the topic of advanced states but the verse makes no claim it addresses.
Siddhi without the body ceasing (தேக மொழியாமல் சித்தி); unrelated to artemisinin.
The verse says wife, sons and house, once real, slipped away as a dream (கனவாய்) within maya's appearances (உருவெளித்தோற்றம்); predictive perception shares only a loose theme of appearances.

The verse argues against caste from the body: the same senses (ஐம்புலன்கள்), the same birth from the womb (யோனியில் பிறந்து), the same food, sleep and pleasure for you and me (உமக்கெனக்கும் ஒக்குமே); the finding that Indian groups share mixed ancestry and that strict endogamy is relatively recent bears on and broadly supports the claim that caste is not a difference of kind, though the verse does not speak of descent.
The verse calls the body a rice-bag and filthy inert matter (ஊத்தைச் சடம்); cell turnover shares only the topic of the body's material.
The verse asks where boiled-away water went, a figure for what vanishes into the mind (மனத்துள்ளே கரந்ததோ); no claim about perception as prediction.
The verse describes drawing breath with the nose (மூக்கால்) and turning the tongue, and admits failure; it claims nothing about memory or fear timed to nasal inhalation.
Alchemists melting cinnabar (லிங்கம்) and the lead-gold fraud; nothing about microbes.
The jnani is indifferent to sleep, waking or awareness withdrawing (உணர்வுசென்று ஒடுங்கிலென்); it makes no claim about the mechanism of unconsciousness.

The verse says that if the mind is right (மனமது செம்மை) there is no need to raise the air or halt the vaasi (வாசியை நிறுத்த வேண்டா); it does not deny breath control has effects, so the finding on slow breathing and arousal is only topical.
The Lord known by the inner eye, pervading like a lamp flame (விளக்குச்சுடரொளி); a simile, not a report of perceived lights in meditation.
Desire trampled as a sandal (ஆசையென்னுஞ் செருப்பு) and ego burnt; no claim about hedonic set points.
A syllable allegory of the snake through the pranava and the mantra (மந்திரத்தை); mantra is shared, but no claim about recitation, breathing or baroreflex.

The verse names a red flame, light and nada (செஞ்சுடர், சோதி, நாதம்) and fear and trembling (நடுங்கி); these overlap with reported meditative lights and fear, but the stanza is obscure and makes no claim the finding tests.
The verse catalogues the body as a cage of death and seat of disease (மரணப் பஞ்சரம், ஓயா நோய்க்கிடம்); cell renewal shares only the body topic.

The verse mocks yogis who levitate and learn the eight siddhis as an art (அட்டசித்து வித்தை) before falling to lust and death; its point is their downfall, and lab failures to replicate precognition share only the topic of powers.
The verse says the dirt in the mind (மனத்தகத்து அழுக்கு), not forest or silence, divides yogis; meditation and the default mode network share the topic but no claim is tested.

reason: Stations of Vishnu and Rudra passed in the ascent; nothing about body clocks.
The verse turns on the flowers of desire (காமமலர்) and the strength of the bond; craving is the shared topic, but the verse makes no claim about wanting and liking.
Life's stages (வாலை, பக்குவம், கிழம்) as the Lord; nothing about hippocampal neurogenesis.

The verse searches hair, skin, blood, bone, marrow and nerves (நரம்பின் கயிறோ) for the self and does not find it; the insula finding on bodily feeling and self shares the topic, but the verse's point is that the self is given by grace.
The twelve-legged horse (பன்னிரண்டு கால்புரவி) bound in two chains is the breath only by cipher; no claim about breathing rate or HRV.
The verse says the body is impermanent (அநித்தியமானது தேகம்); cell turnover shares the body topic but does not test impermanence in the verse's sense.
The guru answers to no law but his own (தன்னாணை); nothing about ageing.
The verse lists the unspoken three-letter mantra (அசவை) among things that are Sivayam; silent repetition is the shared topic, but the ajapa reading is a gloss and the verse claims no effect.
The great medicine (பெருமருந்து) here is opening the mind's lock to end birth and death, not a drug; no claim about depression.
